- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

content.content:
---
name: db-schema-drift-fk-sequences
description: Latent DB bug — FK columns have rogue auto-increment sequences; db:push unsafe (drift vs main)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: db0c107b-d45d-4610-b215-84091dd80729
---

Discovered 2026-06-17 while trying to `db:push` the trades schema. Two drift issues in the live Postgres DB:

**1. Latent bug — foreign-key columns created as `serial` (own auto-increment sequence):**
- `transactions.merchant_id` → `nextval('transactions_merchant_id_seq')`
- `platform_fees.transaction_id` → `nextval('platform_fees_transaction_id_seq')`
- `refunds.transaction_id` → `nextval('refunds_transaction_id_seq')`
A FK should never auto-increment. Schema correctly declares them plain `integer().references(...)`, so drizzle-kit flags a "serial→integer" change (its fix is right, but db:push does it destructively → truncate warning). **Impact verified harmless so far:** transactions_merchant_id_seq is at last_value=1, is_called=false (never fired); 0 orphan transactions — every insert has supplied merchant_id explicitly. Dormant landmine: a future insert omitting merchant_id would silently get 1,2,3… mis-linking to the wrong merchant.
**Safe fix (zero data loss, own small PR against main):** `ALTER TABLE transactions ALTER COLUMN merchant_id DROP DEFAULT;` (+ the other two). Drops only the sequence default.

**2. `main` is behind the live DB:** `invoices_rent_requests.scheduled_send_at` exists in the DB (applied by split-bill work) but not in main's schema. So main-based branches are behind reality.

**Consequence / rule:** do NOT run `npm run db:push` from a main-based branch — it wants to drop scheduled_send_at + truncate tables for the serial→integer changes. Apply schema changes via explicit additive numbered migrations in `migrations/` instead. Get main current with split-bill before any push. Related: [[trades-vertical-project]].

2	-- numbering. Apply only after the Phase 0 first-free allocator is deployed.
3	-- This migration is additive and intentionally performs no data remediation.
4	
5	BEGIN;
6	
7	-- The additive 0010a baseline reconciliation must run first. Refuse to partially
8	-- apply 0011 if the two existing tables this migration must constrain are absent.
9	DO $$
10	BEGIN
11	  IF to_regclass('tapt_stones') IS NULL OR to_regclass('split_payments') IS NULL THEN
12	    RAISE EXCEPTION

15	        'Reconcile the pre-0011 migration baseline with the deployed schema; do not use db:push.';
16	  END IF;
17	END
18	$$;
19	
20	ALTER TABLE transactions
21	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS payment_token_hash text;
22	
23	DO $$
24	BEGIN
25	  IF NOT EXISTS (
26	    SELECT 1
27	    FROM pg_constraint
28	    WHERE conname = 'transactions_payment_token_hash_shape_check'
29	      AND conrelid = 'transactions'::regclass
30	  ) THEN
31	    ALTER TABLE transactions
32	      ADD CONSTRAINT transactions_payment_token_hash_shape_check
33	      CHECK (
34	        payment_token_hash IS NULL
35	        OR payment_token_hash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'
36	      );
37	  END IF;
38	END
39	$$;

42	  ON transactions (payment_token_hash)
43	  WHERE payment_token_hash IS NOT NULL;

46	-- unexpected pre-existing table must abort instead of silently keeping a shape

-- Per-payment credentials, durable payment attempts, and concurrency-safe board
-- numbering. Apply only after the Phase 0 first-free allocator is deployed.
-- This migration is additive and intentionally performs no data remediation.

BEGIN;

-- The additive 0010a baseline reconciliation must run first. Refuse to partially
-- apply 0011 if the two existing tables this migration must constrain are absent.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF to_regclass('tapt_stones') IS NULL OR to_regclass('split_payments') IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      '0011 prerequisites are missing (tapt_stones and/or split_payments)'
      USING HINT =
        'Reconcile the pre-0011 migration baseline with the deployed schema; do not use db:push.';
  END IF;
END
$$;

ALTER TABLE transactions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS payment_token_hash text;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conname = 'transactions_payment_token_hash_shape_check'
      AND conrelid = 'transactions'::regclass
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE transactions
      ADD CONSTRAINT transactions_payment_token_hash_shape_check
      CHECK (
        payment_token_hash IS NULL
        OR payment_token_hash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'
      );
  END IF;
END
$$;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS transactions_payment_token_hash_uq
  ON transactions (payment_token_hash)
  WHERE payment_token_hash IS NOT NULL;

-- This is a new security-sensitive table. Plain CREATE is intentional: an
-- unexpected pre-existing table must abort instead of silently keeping a shape
-- that lacks one of the constraints below.
CREATE TABLE payment_attempts (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  transaction_id integer NOT NULL
    REFERENCES transactions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  share_index integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  idempotency_key uuid NOT NULL,
  state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claiming',
  lease_expires_at timestamp NOT NULL,
  processor_session_id text,
  processor_x_id text,
  return_state_hash text,
  return_state_expires_at timestamp,
  outcome text,
  receipt_share integer,
  created_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_share_index_check
    CHECK (share_index >= 0),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_state_check
    CHECK (
      state IN (
        'claiming',
        'ready',
        'finalizing',
        'approved',
        'declined',
        'cancelled',
        'abandoned'
      )
    ),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_lease_expiry_check
    CHECK (
      lease_expires_at > created_at
      AND lease_expires_at <= created_at + interval '5 minutes'
    ),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_return_state_pair_check
    CHECK (
      (return_state_hash IS NULL) = (return_state_expires_at IS NULL)
    ),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_return_state_hash_shape_check
    CHECK (
      return_state_hash IS NULL
      OR return_state_hash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'
    ),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_return_state_expiry_check
    CHECK (
      return_state_expires_at IS NULL
      OR (
        return_state_expires_at > created_at
        AND return_state_expires_at <= created_at + interval '30 minutes'
      )
    ),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_outcome_check
    CHECK (
      outcome IS NULL
      OR (
        outcome IN ('approved', 'declined', 'cancelled')
        AND state = outcome
      )
    ),
  CONSTRAINT payment_attempts_receipt_share_check
    CHECK (
      receipt_share IS NULL
      OR (share_index >= 1 AND receipt_share = share_index)
    )
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS payment_attempts_transaction_idx
  ON payment_attempts (transaction_id);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS payment_attempts_transaction_share_key_uq
  ON payment_attempts (transaction_id, share_index, idempotency_key);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS payment_attempts_live_transaction_share_uq
  ON payment_attempts (transaction_id, share_index)
  WHERE state IN ('claiming', 'ready', 'finalizing');

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS payment_attempts_return_state_hash_uq
  ON payment_attempts (return_state_hash)
  WHERE return_state_hash IS NOT NULL;

-- Freeze parent/share membership while the read-only audit, NOT NULL hardening,
-- and unique-index build run. Existing rows are never modified or removed.
LOCK TABLE split_payments IN SHARE MODE;

DO $$
DECLARE
  null_parent_count bigint;
  duplicate_detail text;
BEGIN
  SELECT count(*)
  INTO null_parent_count
  FROM split_payments
  WHERE transaction_id IS NULL;

  IF null_parent_count > 0 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      '0011 aborted: split payment rows without a transaction parent exist'
      USING DETAIL = format('rows=%s', null_parent_count),
            HINT =
              'Reconcile these monetary rows from evidence; this migration performs no remediation.';
  END IF;

  SELECT string_agg(
    format(
      'transaction_id=%s split_index=%s rows=%s',
      transaction_id,
      split_index,
      duplicate_count
    ),
    '; ' ORDER BY transaction_id, split_index
  )
  INTO duplicate_detail
  FROM (
    SELECT transaction_id, split_index, count(*) AS duplicate_count
    FROM split_payments
    GROUP BY transaction_id, split_index
    HAVING count(*) > 1
    ORDER BY transaction_id, split_index
    LIMIT 20
  ) duplicates;

  IF duplicate_detail IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      '0011 aborted: duplicate transaction-local split indexes exist'
      USING DETAIL = duplicate_detail,
            HINT =
              'Reconcile these monetary rows from evidence; this migration performs no remediation.';
  END IF;
END
$$;

ALTER TABLE split_payments
  ALTER COLUMN transaction_id SET NOT NULL;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS split_payments_transaction_split_uq
  ON split_payments (transaction_id, split_index);

-- Read-only duplicate-active-board preflight. The index below treats NULL
-- merchant IDs as distinct, so the audit matches its exact conflict domain.
-- No row is renamed, renumbered, deactivated, or deleted by this migration.
LOCK TABLE tapt_stones IN SHARE MODE;

DO $$
DECLARE
  duplicate_detail text;
BEGIN
  SELECT string_agg(
    format(
      'merchant_id=%s stone_number=%s rows=%s',
      merchant_id,
      stone_number,
      duplicate_count
    ),
    '; ' ORDER BY merchant_id, stone_number
  )
  INTO duplicate_detail
  FROM (
    SELECT merchant_id, stone_number, count(*) AS duplicate_count
    FROM tapt_stones
    WHERE is_active IS TRUE
      AND merchant_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY merchant_id, stone_number
    HAVING count(*) > 1
    ORDER BY merchant_id, stone_number
    LIMIT 20
  ) duplicates;

  IF duplicate_detail IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      '0011 aborted: duplicate active payment-board numbers exist'
      USING DETAIL = duplicate_detail,
            HINT =
              'Run the read-only audit, reconcile from evidence, then retry. This migration performs no remediation.';
  END IF;
END
$$;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tapt_stones_active_merchant_number_uq
  ON tapt_stones (merchant_id, stone_number)
  WHERE is_active IS TRUE;

COMMIT;

1	-- Subscription-only pricing: seat-priced monthly plans replace per-transaction
2	-- fees, and users become the canonical login identities behind those seats.
3	--
4	-- This migration is additive and safe to re-run. Historical fee/accounting
5	-- columns and rows remain in place; only defaults for future writes change.
6	
7	BEGIN;
8	
9	-- Remember which subscription rows pre-date the plan columns. The plan columns
10	-- are deliberately introduced nullable and receive defaults only after this
11	-- snapshot, so a rerun cannot reset a customer who subsequently chose Team or
12	-- Crew back to Solo.
13	CREATE TEMP TABLE _taptpay_0013_legacy_subscriptions (
14	  id integer PRIMARY KEY
15	) ON COMMIT DROP;
16	
17	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
18	-- 1. Merchant subscriptions and monthly billing reconciliation
19	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
20	
21	ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
22	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS plan_id text,
23	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS seat_limit integer,
24	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS price_cents integer,
25	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS current_period_start timestamp,
26	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS current_period_end timestamp,
27	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pending_plan_id text,
28	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pending_plan_effective_at timestamp,

42	SELECT id
43	FROM merchant_subscriptions
44	WHERE plan_id IS NULL OR seat_limit IS NULL OR price_cents IS NULL;

47	-- default. Periods begin only after an initial successful subscription charge.
48	ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
49	  ALTER COLUMN current_period_start DROP DEFAULT;
50	
51	-- An older status constraint did not include pending. Remove it before moving
52	-- unverified merchants into the pending state; the complete constraint is added
53	-- back after all data is normalised.

56	
57	UPDATE merchant_subscriptions AS subscription
58	SET plan_id = 'solo',
59	    seat_limit = 1,
60	    price_cents = 799,
61	    status = 'pending',
62	    last_billing_date = NULL,

83	-- a cancellation. Every captured row starts a fresh paid period only after card

-- Subscription-only pricing: seat-priced monthly plans replace per-transaction
-- fees, and users become the canonical login identities behind those seats.
--
-- This migration is additive and safe to re-run. Historical fee/accounting
-- columns and rows remain in place; only defaults for future writes change.

BEGIN;

-- Remember which subscription rows pre-date the plan columns. The plan columns
-- are deliberately introduced nullable and receive defaults only after this
-- snapshot, so a rerun cannot reset a customer who subsequently chose Team or
-- Crew back to Solo.
CREATE TEMP TABLE _taptpay_0013_legacy_subscriptions (
  id integer PRIMARY KEY
) ON COMMIT DROP;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Merchant subscriptions and monthly billing reconciliation
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS plan_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS seat_limit integer,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS price_cents integer,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS current_period_start timestamp,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS current_period_end timestamp,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pending_plan_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pending_plan_effective_at timestamp,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cancel_at_period_end boolean,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS windcave_card_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS windcave_billing_ref text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS card_brand text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS card_last4 text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS card_expiry text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS failed_payment_count integer,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_payment_failure_at timestamp,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_payment_failure_reason text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS billing_claim_token text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS billing_claimed_at timestamp;

INSERT INTO _taptpay_0013_legacy_subscriptions (id)
SELECT id
FROM merchant_subscriptions
WHERE plan_id IS NULL OR seat_limit IS NULL OR price_cents IS NULL;

-- A previous version of this migration briefly gave current_period_start a
-- default. Periods begin only after an initial successful subscription charge.
ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
  ALTER COLUMN current_period_start DROP DEFAULT;

-- An older status constraint did not include pending. Remove it before moving
-- unverified merchants into the pending state; the complete constraint is added
-- back after all data is normalised.
ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS merchant_subscriptions_status_check;

UPDATE merchant_subscriptions AS subscription
SET plan_id = 'solo',
    seat_limit = 1,
    price_cents = 799,
    status = 'pending',
    last_billing_date = NULL,
    current_period_start = NULL,
    current_period_end = NULL,
    next_billing_date = NULL,
    pending_plan_id = NULL,
    pending_plan_effective_at = NULL,
    cancel_at_period_end = false,
    cancellation_requested_at = NULL,
    cancellation_effective_date = NULL,
    cancellation_reason = NULL,
    failed_payment_count = 0,
    last_payment_failure_at = NULL,
    last_payment_failure_reason = NULL,
    billing_claim_token = NULL,
    billing_claimed_at = NULL
FROM _taptpay_0013_legacy_subscriptions AS legacy
WHERE subscription.id = legacy.id;

-- Legacy rows belonged to the retired per-transaction fee sweeper. Their
-- status, last_billing_date and cancellation dates do not describe a paid seat
-- subscription and must never grant access, skip the initial charge, or inherit
-- a cancellation. Every captured row starts a fresh paid period only after card
-- activation succeeds.

-- Repair only invalid/incomplete rows. Valid rows are never re-priced on a
-- rerun, which is essential once merchants can change plan after deployment.
UPDATE merchant_subscriptions
SET plan_id = 'solo', seat_limit = 1, price_cents = 799
WHERE plan_id IS NULL
   OR plan_id NOT IN ('solo', 'team', 'crew')
   OR seat_limit IS NULL
   OR seat_limit < 1
   OR price_cents IS NULL
   OR price_cents < 0;

UPDATE merchant_subscriptions
SET status = 'pending'
WHERE status IS NULL
   OR status NOT IN ('pending', 'active', 'past_due', 'suspended', 'cancelled');

UPDATE merchant_subscriptions
SET cancel_at_period_end = false
WHERE cancel_at_period_end IS NULL;

UPDATE merchant_subscriptions
SET failed_payment_count = 0
WHERE failed_payment_count IS NULL OR failed_payment_count < 0;

ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
  ALTER COLUMN plan_id SET DEFAULT 'solo',
  ALTER COLUMN plan_id SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN seat_limit SET DEFAULT 1,
  ALTER COLUMN seat_limit SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN price_cents SET DEFAULT 799,
  ALTER COLUMN price_cents SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'pending',
  ALTER COLUMN cancel_at_period_end SET DEFAULT false,
  ALTER COLUMN cancel_at_period_end SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN failed_payment_count SET DEFAULT 0,
  ALTER COLUMN failed_payment_count SET NOT NULL;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conname = 'merchant_subscriptions_plan_id_check'
      AND conrelid = 'merchant_subscriptions'::regclass
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT merchant_subscriptions_plan_id_check
      CHECK (plan_id IN ('solo', 'team', 'crew'));
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conname = 'merchant_subscriptions_pending_plan_id_check'
      AND conrelid = 'merchant_subscriptions'::regclass
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT merchant_subscriptions_pending_plan_id_check
      CHECK (pending_plan_id IS NULL OR pending_plan_id IN ('solo', 'team', 'crew'));
  END IF;

  ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
    ADD CONSTRAINT merchant_subscriptions_status_check
    CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'active', 'past_due', 'suspended', 'cancelled'));

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conname = 'merchant_subscriptions_seat_limit_check'
      AND conrelid = 'merchant_subscriptions'::regclass
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT merchant_subscriptions_seat_limit_check CHECK (seat_limit >= 1);
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conname = 'merchant_subscriptions_price_cents_check'
      AND conrelid = 'merchant_subscriptions'::regclass
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE merchant_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT merchant_subscriptions_price_cents_check CHECK (price_cents >= 0);
  END IF;
END $$;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS subscription_billing_history (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  merchant_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES merchants(id),
  subscription_id integer REFERENCES merchant_subscriptions(id),
  billing_type text NOT NULL,
  amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  transaction_count integer DEFAULT 0,
  billing_period_start timestamp,
  billing_period_end timestamp,
  stripe_payment_intent_id text,
  stripe_charge_id text,
  windcave_transaction_id text,
  idempotency_key text,
  attempt_number integer,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  description text,
  failure_reason text,
  paid_at timestamp,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE subscription_billing_history
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS windcave_transaction_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS idempotency_key text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS attempt_number integer;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS subscription_billing_history_merchant_created_idx
  ON subscription_billing_history (merchant_id, created_at);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS subscription_billing_history_idempotency_key_uq
  ON subscription_billing_history (idempotency_key)
  WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL;

-- The transaction fee is historical only. Preserve old values but make every
-- future transaction default to zero if a caller omits the explicit rate.
ALTER TABLE transactions
  ALTER COLUMN platform_fee_rate SET DEFAULT '0.0000';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Users: canonical login identity and one deterministic owner per merchant
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ALTER TABLE users
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS name text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS status text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS invite_token_hash text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS invite_expires_at timestamp,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_login_at timestamp,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reset_token text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reset_token_expiry timestamp;

-- Migration 0000 accidentally made this foreign key serial/not-null. Platform
-- administrators have no merchant and must not consume a merchant sequence.
ALTER TABLE users
  ALTER COLUMN merchant_id DROP DEFAULT,
  ALTER COLUMN merchant_id DROP NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN role SET DEFAULT 'member';

ALTER TABLE users
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS users_role_check,
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS users_status_check;

UPDATE users
SET role = 'member'
WHERE role IS NULL OR role NOT IN ('owner', 'member', 'admin');

UPDATE users
SET status = 'active'
WHERE status IS NULL OR status NOT IN ('active', 'invited', 'disabled');

ALTER TABLE users
  ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'active',
  ALTER COLUMN status SET NOT NULL;

-- Fail safely instead of letting a case-only duplicate make login routing
-- ambiguous. The exception identifies the data cleanup needed before retrying.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT lower(email)
    FROM users
    GROUP BY lower(email)
    HAVING count(*) > 1
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION '0013 cannot enforce case-insensitive user email uniqueness: duplicate lower(email) values exist';
  END IF;
END $$;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_email_lower_uq
  ON users (lower(email));

-- Retain exactly one existing non-admin identity as owner for each merchant.
-- Password-enabled merchants must use the identity matching the merchant email;
-- otherwise the old merchant credentials would stop working. For a legacy
-- merchant without a password, prefer an email match, then an existing owner,
-- then the oldest row. The CTE snapshots the old roles before the update.
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT user_row.id,
         merchant.password_hash,
         lower(user_row.email) = lower(merchant.email) AS email_matches,
         row_number() OVER (
           PARTITION BY user_row.merchant_id
           ORDER BY
             (lower(user_row.email) = lower(merchant.email)) DESC,
             (user_row.role = 'owner') DESC,
             user_row.id
         ) AS owner_rank
  FROM users AS user_row
  JOIN merchants AS merchant ON merchant.id = user_row.merchant_id
  WHERE user_row.role <> 'admin'
)
UPDATE users AS user_row
SET role = CASE
  WHEN ranked.password_hash IS NOT NULL AND ranked.email_matches THEN 'owner'
  WHEN ranked.password_hash IS NULL AND ranked.owner_rank = 1 THEN 'owner'
  ELSE 'member'
END
FROM ranked
WHERE user_row.id = ranked.id;

-- Keep a pre-existing matching identity's password aligned with the merchant
-- credential. Missing matching identities are inserted immediately below.
UPDATE users AS owner_row
SET password = merchant.password_hash,
    status = 'active',
    name = COALESCE(owner_row.name, merchant.name)
FROM merchants AS merchant
WHERE owner_row.merchant_id = merchant.id
  AND owner_row.role = 'owner'
  AND merchant.password_hash IS NOT NULL
  AND lower(owner_row.email) = lower(merchant.email);

-- Merchants already able to sign in receive the owner identity they previously
-- used implicitly. ON CONFLICT makes the insert re-runnable; the assertion below
-- prevents a cross-merchant email collision from silently leaving no owner.
INSERT INTO users (email, password, merchant_id, role, status, name, created_at)
SELECT merchant.email,
       merchant.password_hash,
       merchant.id,
       'owner',
       'active',
       merchant.name,
       COALESCE(merchant.created_at, now())
FROM merchants AS merchant
WHERE merchant.password_hash IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM users AS owner_row
    WHERE owner_row.merchant_id = merchant.id AND owner_row.role = 'owner'
  )
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM merchants AS merchant
    WHERE merchant.password_hash IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM users AS owner_row
        WHERE owner_row.merchant_id = merchant.id AND owner_row.role = 'owner'
      )
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION '0013 could not create an owner identity for every password-enabled merchant';
  END IF;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_merchant_id_idx ON users (merchant_id);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_invite_token_hash_uq
  ON users (invite_token_hash)
  WHERE invite_token_hash IS NOT NULL;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_reset_token_hash_uq
  ON users (reset_token)
  WHERE reset_token IS NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE users
  ADD CONSTRAINT users_role_check
  CHECK (role IN ('owner', 'member', 'admin')),
  ADD CONSTRAINT users_status_check
  CHECK (status IN ('active', 'invited', 'disabled'));

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Seed a subscription for every merchant that still lacks one
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

INSERT INTO merchant_subscriptions (
  merchant_id, plan_id, seat_limit, price_cents, status,
  current_period_start, current_period_end, next_billing_date,
  cancel_at_period_end, failed_payment_count,
  month_start_date, created_at, updated_at
)
SELECT merchant.id,
       'solo',
       1,
       799,
       'pending',
       NULL,
       NULL,
       NULL,
       false,
       0,
       now(),
       now(),
       now()
FROM merchants AS merchant
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM merchant_subscriptions AS subscription
  WHERE subscription.merchant_id = merchant.id
);

COMMIT;

---
name: dev-db-unapplied-migrations
description: Dev DB was 3 migrations behind, hanging /api/auth/me and bricking the whole app; fixed 2026-08-09 + how to re-diagnose
metadata:
  type: project
---

**2026-08-09: "app just loads forever after login" on desktop AND mobile.** Root cause was
the dev database (helium), not the UI.

`shared/schema.ts` had run ahead of the dev DB: migrations **0011, 0012, 0013 were never
applied** there. Drizzle's `select()` enumerates every declared column, so
`getOrCreateSubscription()` issued `select … billing_claim_token …` against a table without
it → Postgres `42703 undefined_column`.

**Why that bricked the entire app rather than showing an error:** `/api/auth/me` had no
try/catch, and Express 4 does not route an async rejection to the error handler — so the
request stayed open forever. `AuthProvider` in `client/src/App.tsx` gates first paint on that
one call (`isChecking` only clears in `.finally()`), so every device class sat on `PageLoader`
indefinitely. Fixed by wrapping the handler (uncommitted on `feat/tablet-desktop-app`).
**~25 other async handlers in `server/routes.ts` still lack try/catch** — same hang is
reachable through any of them.

**Applied fix:** ran 0011/0012/0013 with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`. They are additive and
re-runnable; verified first that 0013's destructive `UPDATE` matched 0 rows and no user's
role would flip. Drift went 2 missing tables + 7 missing columns → 0.

**Re-diagnosing drift (the reliable way):** `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` is EMPTY on dev —
the DB was built by `db:push`, so applied-state cannot be read from it. Instead diff
`getTableConfig()` over every export of `shared/schema.ts` against `information_schema.columns`.
Do NOT `npm run db:push` — see [[db-schema-drift-fk-sequences]].

Also note `pg_stat_activity.state` is `'disabled'` on this Neon instance (track_activities off),
so it cannot be used to prove "no query is running". Related: [[data-persistence-topology]],
[[playwright-nix-chromium]], [[server-crash-hardening]].

content.text:
Found and fixed it. The problem was in the dev **database**, not the UI.

## What was wrong

Your dev database was three migrations behind `shared/schema.ts`, and one missing column took the whole app down:

1. Migrations **0011, 0012, 0013 were never applied** to the dev DB (helium). `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` is empty — the DB was built by `db:push`, so nothing tracked it.
2. `merchant_subscriptions` was missing `billing_claim_token` / `billing_claimed_at` (added by the C5 cron-race fix).
3. Drizzle's `select()` enumerates *every* declared column, so `getOrCreateSubscription()` hit Postgres error `42703: column "billing_claim_token" does not exist`.
4. `/api/auth/me` had **no try/catch**, and Express 4 doesn't route async rejections to the error handler — so the request was never answered. It hung indefinitely (I let a curl sit on it for 2 minutes).
5. `AuthProvider` (`client/src/App.tsx:220`) gates first paint on that single call — `isChecking` only clears in `.finally()`. So every device class sat on `PageLoader` forever. That's why desktop, tablet **and** mobile were all identically stuck.

The full drift was 2 missing tables (`payment_attempts`, `push_notification_deliveries`) and 7 missing columns — `transactions.payment_token_hash` was also why `/api/merchants/22/transactions` was returning 500.

## What I did

**Applied migrations 0011/0012/0013** — no `db:push`, per your FK-sequence rule. I checked the abort conditions and data risks first: 0013's destructive `UPDATE` matched **0 rows**, no user's role would flip, no duplicate emails/board numbers. Backup taken beforehand at `…/scratchpad/dev-db-backup-20260809-052250.sql`.

**Wrapped `/api/auth/me` in try/catch** (`server/routes.ts:770`) — indentation plus the wrapper, no logic change. A backend failure there should return an error, not silently brick every client.

## Verified

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/auth/me` | hang (>2 min) | 200 in 30ms |
| `/api/merchants/22/transactions` | 500 | 200 |
| schema drift | 2 tables, 7 columns | 0 |

App loads on mobile/tablet/desktop across `/dashboard`, `/terminal`, `/transactions` — screenshots show the real dashboard with merchant 22's actual transactions. The only console error left is Replit's own dev-banner script 403ing. `tsc` clean, 188/188 server tests pass.

I also re-created the exact fault (renamed the column, then restored it) to prove the hang is gone: it now returns 500 in 36ms instead of hanging.

## Worth knowing

- **~25 other async handlers in `server/routes.ts` still lack try/catch** — including `/api/pay/t/:token/*` and `/api/billing/card`. The same infinite-hang is reachable through any of them. A router-level async wrapper would close this class off properly; I didn't do it since it changes error semantics across 198 routes and that's your call.
- **Production may have the same drift.** I only touched dev. Worth checking prod before the next deploy — if prod is also missing these, `/api/auth/me` will hang there too.
- The `server/routes.ts` change is **uncommitted**, sitting alongside your landing-phone work.

Done. First, a correction to my earlier number.

## It's 5, not 25

My earlier count came from a regex that only checked whether `try` appeared in the first line of each handler. Most of those 25 do have try/catch, just not on line one. I redid it as an AST pass over all 204 async handlers, looking for `await`s that sit outside any `try` with a `catch` — that found **5** genuinely exposed handlers.

## The five

| Endpoint | Where it leaked | What it meant |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/billing/card` | `getMerchant`, `getOrCreateSubscription` | **Same shape as the `/api/auth/me` bug** — it calls the same `getOrCreateSubscription`. Settings → Billing would have hung during today's outage too. Its sibling `POST /api/billing/card/session` was already wrapped, so this was an inconsistency. |
| `POST /api/v1/transactions` | `logApiRequest` **inside the catch** | The public API hangs precisely when the DB is broken — the audit write throws on the way to sending the 500/503, so the client gets nothing at all instead of an error. |
| `GET /api/v1/transactions/:id` | same | same |
| `GET /api/merchants/:id/events` | `authenticateToken`, `getTaptStone` | SSE. A throw before the stream opens leaves `EventSource` waiting on a socket that never answers, so it never even reaches its retry path. |
| `GET /api/auth/validate-reset-token/:token` | whole body unguarded | Password-reset page hangs. |

The two v1 cases are the nastiest: the failure is *in the error handler*, so it only bites during an outage — exactly when you need the error message.

## What wasn't a problem

The 9 "catch never responds" hits were all false positives from my checker. The webhooks (`/api/pay/notification`, `/api/windcave/*`, `/api/webhooks/whatsapp`) deliberately `res.status(200).send("OK")` *before* the try so the provider stops retrying, and the rest are inner catches around optional sub-steps (email send, user creation) where the outer handler still replies.

I also checked two things the scan could have missed: `authenticateToken` — async and on nearly every route — is properly guarded, and the two by-name handlers (`billingCardCallback`) are synchronous.

## Fixed and verified

All five wrapped. The diff is **purely additive**: `git diff -w` shows **0 removed lines**, everything else is re-indentation.

- AST re-scan: **0 unguarded awaits** across 204 handlers
- `tsc` clean, 188/188 server tests pass
- Fault injection — I hid `billing_claim_token` and `tapt_stones.stone_number` again, and all three affected endpoints returned **500 in under 100ms** where they previously hung indefinitely; DB restored, 0 leftover columns

The SSE fix needed a different shape from the rest: once `writeHead` has fired, a JSON body would corrupt the stream, so its catch ends the socket instead and lets `EventSource` reconnect on its own schedule.

## One thing I'd still flag

This was a snapshot fix — route #205 can reintroduce it. The permanent version is a router-level shim that attaches `.catch(next)` to any promise a handler returns, which routes rejections into your existing error handler at `server/index.ts:305`. That handler already checks `!res.headersSent` before replying, so the fast-ack webhooks and the SSE stream would just log rather than double-send. It's maybe 15 lines and would make this class of bug unreachable.

I didn't do it — it changes the rejection path for all 204 handlers at once, and given this branch's design-deviation process that felt like your call rather than mine. Say the word and I'll add it.

Separately, worth knowing: when the DB is down, `authenticateToken` catches and returns `404 User not found`, which the client reads as a dead session and bounces to login. Not a hang, but during an outage it looks to a merchant like their account was deleted.

47	-   `Merchants` table: Stores merchant details, including business name, email, director, address, NZBN, phone, GST number, Windcave API key, custom logo URL, and QR/payment URLs.
48	-   `Transactions` table: Records transaction details, status, external processor IDs, and fee breakdowns (Windcave, Platform, Merchant net).

53	-   **Transaction Creation:** Merchant input via terminal (with optional Split Bill toggle) -> Frontend validation -> Backend creates transaction in DB with `splitEnabled` flag -> QR code generation -> SSE notification.

55	-   **Split Bill Flow:** Merchant toggles "Split Bill" on before creating transaction -> Customer opens payment URL -> Redirected to `/split/:transactionId` -> Customer chooses number of splits (2-10) -> `POST /api/transactions/:id/split` sets `isSplit=true` -> Each person goes through Windcave HPP for their share -> After each payment, callback redirects to `/receipt/:id?splitId=X` where each payer receives their individual receipt.
56	-   **Receipt Flow:** After successful payment, customer is redirected to `/receipt/:transactionId` (optionally with `?splitId=X` for split payments). Receipt shows full business info (name, GST number, NZBN, address), itemised breakdown, GST calculation (15% NZ), total, and PDF download + Share buttons. Web Share API used for sharing — shares the PDF file on mobile, falls back to link sharing on desktop. Failed/cancelled payments show "Try Again" button on `/payment/result/:id?status=declined|cancelled`.
57	-   **Real-time Updates:** SSE connections per merchant for immediate transaction status broadcasts to both merchant and customer interfaces.
58	-   **Push Notifications:** On transaction status changes (created, completed, failed, refunded), push notifications sent to all active subscriptions for the merchant via Web Push API. Merchants enable/disable in Settings page.

61	-   Authentication: JWT-based, protected routes, session management.
62	-   Admin Authentication: Configurable via ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH env vars. Admin login disabled if ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH not set. Uses bcrypt for password verification.
63	-   Merchant Route Authorization: All merchant data routes enforce ownership checks via `checkMerchantOwnership()` helper - admins can access all merchants, regular users can only access their own merchant data.

70	    -   Payment endpoint verification: Triple verification (transaction→merchant, transaction→stone, stone→merchant) with Zod schema validation blocks cross-stone and cross-merchant payment tampering.

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
fix(api): answer the request when a handler throws, instead of hanging

Express 4 does not route an async handler's rejection to the error
handler, so an unguarded throw leaves the request open forever. The
client never sees an error — it just waits.

That is how a single missing column took the whole app down: the dev
database was behind on migrations 0011-0013, so getOrCreateSubscription
hit `column "billing_claim_token" does not exist`, /api/auth/me never
answered, and AuthProvider — which gates first paint on that one call —
sat on the full-screen loader on every device class.

An AST pass over all 204 async route handlers found five that could
leak a rejection. All now answer:

- GET  /api/auth/me                        gated first paint everywhere
- GET  /api/billing/card                   same getOrCreateSubscription call
- GET  /api/merchants/:id/events           SSE; a throw before the stream
                                           opened left EventSource waiting
- POST /api/v1/transactions                the unguarded await was *inside*
- GET  /api/v1/transactions/:id            the catch, so the public API hung
                                           precisely when the DB was broken

The SSE handler cannot reply with JSON once its stream is open, so its
catch ends the socket instead and lets EventSource reconnect. The two v1
handlers make their audit write best-effort so the 500/503 always goes
out.

Purely additive: `git diff -w` shows no removed lines. Verified by
re-injecting the original fault — all three affected endpoints now
return 500 in under 100ms where they previously hung indefinitely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

---
name: dev-db-unapplied-migrations
description: 2026-08-09 app-wouldn't-load incident — dev DB was 3 migrations behind; fixed + committed, with 4 open flags for next session
metadata:
  type: project
---

**2026-08-09: "app just loads forever after login" on desktop AND mobile.** Root cause was
the dev database (helium), not the UI.

`shared/schema.ts` had run ahead of the dev DB: migrations **0011, 0012, 0013 were never
applied** there. Drizzle's `select()` enumerates every declared column, so
`getOrCreateSubscription()` issued `select … billing_claim_token …` against a table without
it → Postgres `42703 undefined_column`.

**Why that bricked the whole app rather than showing an error:** Express 4 does not route an
async handler's rejection to the error handler, so the unguarded throw left the request open
forever. `AuthProvider` in `client/src/App.tsx` gates first paint on that single
`/api/auth/me` call (`isChecking` only clears in `.finally()`), so every device class sat on
`PageLoader` indefinitely.

**Fixed and committed as `5022431`** on `feat/tablet-desktop-app`: applied 0011/0012/0013 with
`psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1` (verified first that 0013's destructive `UPDATE` matched 0 rows and
no user's role would flip), and guarded the 5 leaking handlers. Drift went 2 tables + 7 columns
→ 0.

An AST pass over all 204 async handlers found exactly **5** leaks — `/api/auth/me`,
`/api/billing/card`, `/api/merchants/:id/events` (SSE), and both `/api/v1/transactions*`
(their unguarded await sat *inside* the catch, so the public API hung precisely when the DB
was broken). An earlier grep suggested ~25; that was wrong — it only checked whether `try`
appeared on the handler's first line.

## Open flags for next session

1. **HIGHEST — there is no migration runner, and production may be drifted too.** Nothing
   applies `migrations/*.sql`; `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` is empty; the startup
   `drizzle-kit push` is opt-in behind `RUN_SCHEMA_PUSH`/`RUN_MIGRATIONS` (`server/index.ts:142`).
   Only a bespoke `ALTER TABLE merchants ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS …` block runs unconditionally
   (`server/index.ts:178`). **Check prod for the same missing columns before the next deploy** —
   if it is also behind, `/api/auth/me` hangs there exactly as dev did.
2. **Router-level async safety net (~15 lines).** Wrap `app.get/post/…` so a returned promise
   gets `.catch(next)`, routing rejections into the existing error handler at
   `server/index.ts:305`. That handler already checks `!res.headersSent`, so the fast-ack
   webhooks and the SSE stream would only log. Without it, route #205 reintroduces the hang.
   Oliver was asked and had not yet decided when the session ended.
3. **`authenticateToken` reports a DB outage as `404 User not found`** (`server/auth.ts`, the
   catch around the user lookup). The client reads that as a dead session and bounces to
   login — during an outage a merchant sees what looks like a deleted account.
4. **`replit.md` lines 80-82 are stale/wrong** — they claim "the server startup runs
   `drizzle-kit push`", which is what makes people assume new columns auto-apply on restart.
   It is opt-in. See `.agents/memory/schema-push-and-drift.md`, which is correct.

**Re-diagnosing drift (the reliable way):** diff `getTableConfig()` over every export of
`shared/schema.ts` against `information_schema.columns`. Do NOT `npm run db:push` — see
[[db-schema-drift-fk-sequences]]. Note `pg_stat_activity.state` is `'disabled'` on this Neon
instance (track_activities off), so it cannot prove "no query is running".

Related: [[data-persistence-topology]], [[playwright-nix-chromium]], [[server-crash-hardening]].

**2026-08-09: "app just loads forever after login" on desktop AND mobile.** Root cause was
the dev database (helium), not the UI.

`shared/schema.ts` had run ahead of the dev DB: migrations **0011, 0012, 0013 were never
applied** there. Drizzle's `select()` enumerates every declared column, so
`getOrCreateSubscription()` issued `select … billing_claim_token …` against a table without
it → Postgres `42703 undefined_column`.

**Why that bricked the entire app rather than showing an error:** `/api/auth/me` had no
try/catch, and Express 4 does not route an async rejection to the error handler — so the
request stayed open forever. `AuthProvider` in `client/src/App.tsx` gates first paint on that
one call (`isChecking` only clears in `.finally()`), so every device class sat on `PageLoader`
indefinitely. Fixed by wrapping the handler (uncommitted on `feat/tablet-desktop-app`).
**~25 other async handlers in `server/routes.ts` still lack try/catch** — same hang is
reachable through any of them.

**Applied fix:** ran 0011/0012/0013 with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`. They are additive and
re-runnable; verified first that 0013's destructive `UPDATE` matched 0 rows and no user's
role would flip. Drift went 2 missing tables + 7 missing columns → 0.

**Re-diagnosing drift (the reliable way):** `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` is EMPTY on dev —
the DB was built by `db:push`, so applied-state cannot be read from it. Instead diff
`getTableConfig()` over every export of `shared/schema.ts` against `information_schema.columns`.
Do NOT `npm run db:push` — see [[db-schema-drift-fk-sequences]].

Also note `pg_stat_activity.state` is `'disabled'` on this Neon instance (track_activities off),
so it cannot be used to prove "no query is running". Related: [[data-persistence-topology]],
[[playwright-nix-chromium]], [[server-crash-hardening]].

# Background (why this matters)

Yesterday the whole app broke: it hung on a loading spinner after login on every device. Root cause was that the dev database was three migrations behind `shared/schema.ts`. Drizzle's `select()` enumerates every column declared in the schema, so a query hit `column "billing_claim_token" does not exist` and the request died.

The reason it drifted: **there is no migration runner in this project.** The `migrations/*.sql` files are checked in but nothing ever applies them. Evidence:

Build a proper SQL migration runner.

1. **New file `server/migrate.ts`** — a runner that:
   - Reads `migrations/*.sql` in **lexical filename order**.    - Applies only unapplied migrations, **each inside its own transaction**, in order, aborting the whole run on the first failure.    - Detects **checksum drift**: if a file's contents changed after it was recorded as applied, fail loudly with a clear message rather than silently ignoring it.
   - Use the `pg` package (already a dependency) and `process.env.DATABASE_URL`. Do not use `@neondatabase/serverless` for this.

The dev database **already has the effects of all 14 migration files applied** (I verified schema drift is currently zero), but the ledger is empty. If someone runs the runner now it would try to re-execute 0000 onwards, which is not safe for all of them. So provide a baseline mode that records migrations as applied **without executing them**, for adopting the runner on an existing database. Make it explicit and hard to trigger by accident.

3. **`npm run db:migrate` script** in `package.json` (and a separate script for baseline if you prefer). Only touch the `scripts` section.

Respect that policy — the goal is that drift becomes impossible to miss, not that it silently self-heals. Keep it cheap and non-blocking, and make sure it cannot crash startup if the DB is unreachable.

- There is uncommitted work-in-progress under `client/src/pages/landing-phone/**` — do not touch it.
- Do not touch `.claude-home/**` or `.claude/settings.local.json`.

# Verify before you report back

- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `npx jest --selectProjects server --runInBand` passes (188 tests currently pass; keep them all passing plus your new ones).
- Actually exercise the runner against the dev database to prove it works: baseline it, then confirm a subsequent run correctly reports "nothing to apply", and confirm the pending-check reports clean. **Do not let it re-execute the existing migrations.** If you are unsure whether an action is safe against the dev DB, take a `pg_dump` backup first (pg_dump is on PATH) and say so in your report.

# Report back

Give me: the design decisions you made (especially how you handled the embedded BEGIN/COMMIT and the baseline mode), the exact files you changed, the verification output, and anything you found that I should know about. Be honest about anything you could not verify.

You are working in the repo at /home/runner/workspace (branch `feat/tablet-desktop-app`). Node/TypeScript, **Express 4** (4.21.2) + Drizzle ORM.

# Background (why this matters)

Express 4 does **not** route a rejected promise from an async route handler to the error-handling middleware. When an async handler throws, nothing calls `next(err)`, the response is never sent, and the request stays open forever. The client hangs on a spinner with no error.

That exact bug took this whole app down yesterday: a missing database column made `/api/auth/me` throw, the request never answered, and because the React `AuthProvider` gates first paint on that one call, every device class sat on a full-screen loader indefinitely.

I already fixed the five specific handlers that were leaking (committed as `5022431`). But that is a snapshot fix — the 205th route someone writes reintroduces the same class of bug. Your job is to close the class permanently.

# Your task

Add a router-level async safety net.

1. **New file** (name it sensibly, e.g. `server/async-route-guard.ts`) exporting a function that patches an Express app/router so that **any handler returning a promise gets `.catch(next)` attached**. A rejection then flows into the existing global error handler.

   The global error handler already exists at `server/index.ts` around line 305. Read it first. It already checks `!res.headersSent` before responding, which is what makes this safe for the cases below.

2. **Install it** at the very top of `registerRoutes` in `server/routes.ts`, before any route is registered, so every subsequent registration is covered.

**Server** — `authenticateToken` in `server/auth.ts`. It validates the JWT, then looks the user up in the database inside a `try`. So when the database is unreachable, every authenticated request reports **404 User not found** — indistinguishable from a genuinely deleted account.

**Client** — `AuthProvider` in `client/src/App.tsx` (around lines 209-249). Its `.then()` clears `authToken`, `user` and `merchantId` from localStorage on **any** non-ok response, and its `.catch()` does the same on **any** network error. So a transient 500/503, or a dropped wifi connection, silently destroys the merchant's session and dumps them at the login screen.

Combined: during a backend outage a signed-in merchant gets logged out and sees what looks like a deleted account.

# Your task

Make the system distinguish **authentication failure** from **infrastructure failure**, and respond appropriately to each.

**Server side (`server/auth.ts`):**
- A genuine "no such user row" must keep returning 404.
- An infrastructure failure (the DB lookup throwing) must return **503** with a distinct, honest message — not 404, and not a message implying the account is gone.
- Be careful to actually distinguish the two cases rather than blanket-converting the catch: read the existing logic closely. Currently the `try` covers both the lookup and the subsequent validity checks, and several legitimate "not found / revoked" outcomes `return` from inside the `try`.

**Client side (`client/src/App.tsx`):**
- Only clear the stored credentials when the server actually rejects the credentials — **401 / 403**.
- On **5xx or a network error, do NOT clear the token.** The session is probably fine; the backend is not.
- Surface a recoverable state instead of a silent logout — the user should understand that something is wrong on our side and be able to retry, rather than being dumped at a login page that may also fail.

- Every path must terminate in a definite state — signed in, signed out, or a visible error. Never an unbounded wait.

content.text:
Production is done. Let me report while the agents finish.

## Production migrated ✅

| step | result |
|---|---|
| Backup | `pg_dump` → 227K, 29 tables with data (kept in scratchpad) |
| Rehearsal | applied + **rolled back**; prod verified byte-identical afterwards |
| Real run | 0011/0012/0013 in **one** transaction, 403ms |
| Commit gate | transaction only committed after asserting 0 missing tables, 0 unexpected missing columns, every password-enabled merchant has an owner, no subscription without a plan |
| Drift | 2 tables + 31 columns → **0** |

Then I hit something the rehearsal surfaced but didn't block on, and it mattered: after the three migrations, prod still failed a real Drizzle query with `column "business_description" does not exist`. Those three `merchants` columns are only ever created by the boot-time block at `server/index.ts:178` — and because Drizzle's `select()` enumerates every declared column, their absence breaks **every** query on `merchants`. Since `getMerchant()` runs *before* `getOrCreateSubscription()` in `/api/auth/me`, prod would still have failed. I applied that same `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` DDL directly rather than leave prod depending on a boot side-effect.

Verified against prod afterwards with the real Drizzle query path — `getOrCreateSubscription` returns `plan=solo status=pending`, and the `users` select works.

**Two things you should know about prod's new state:**

1. **Merchants can now sign in — they couldn't before.** The `users` table was empty, and auth resolves every token against a `users` row. 0013 created 4 owner identities, all with usable password hashes carried over from `merchants.password_hash` (I checked). Yours is there: `oliverharryleonard@gmail.com` → merchant 22.

2. **All 8 subscriptions are `pending`**, with no `lastBillingDate` or `windcaveCardId`. `billingCardIsReady()` returns false for those, and 16 payment-sending endpoints sit behind `requireBillingCard`. So each merchant must add a card and clear the first charge before they can send payments. That's the designed behaviour of the subscription model, not damage — but it's now live, so it's the first thing you'll hit if you log into prod.

The three agents are still running. I'll report the migration runner, the async safety net, and the auth/outage work as they land, then do the integration pass and commit.

## What I built

**`/home/runner/workspace/server/async-route-guard.ts`** (new) — exports `installAsyncRouteGuard(app)`, plus `wrapAsyncHandler` and an `asyncRouteGuardInternals` bag for tests.

It replaces `get/post/put/patch/delete/all/use` on the target with patched versions that map every argument through a wrapper before delegating to the original method (`originalMethod.apply(this, args.map(guardArgument))`). Functions get wrapped, arrays are mapped recursively (Express flattens handler arrays deeply), and everything else — path strings, RegExps, `express.json({...})` option objects — passes through by identity. The patched method **returns** the original's return value, which is what keeps `app.get("env")` working as Express's settings getter (index.ts:377 depends on it) with no special-casing: one string argument simply has nothing to wrap.

The wrapper calls the handler, and only if the result is a promise does it attach `result.then(undefined, reason => next(...))`. A sync throw is deliberately *not* caught — Express's own `try/catch` in `Layer.handle_request` already forwards it, and intercepting it would change the error semantics of every sync handler.

**`/home/runner/workspace/server/routes.ts`** — 2 additive hunks: the import, and `installAsyncRouteGuard(app);` as the first statement of `registerRoutes` (before `paymentAttempts`, before the first `app.get`).

## Arity detection

I read `node_modules/express/lib/router/layer.js` rather than working from memory. Express switches on arity in two places: `handle_error` skips anything where `fn.length !== 4`, and `handle_request` skips anything where `fn.length > 3`. So:

- **Anything with `length >= 4` is returned untouched** — that covers real error middleware and also `length > 4` functions, which Express treats as dead layers. Wrapping a 5-arity function with a 3-arity wrapper would have *revived* a dead layer, so `>= 4` is the correct cutoff, not `=== 4`.
- **Wrapped handlers report the original arity exactly**, via `Object.defineProperty(guarded, "length", { value: handler.length })`. The wrapper uses rest args (so it forwards all arguments and preserves `this` via `.apply`), which would otherwise report `length === 0`; restoring the real length means a 0-, 1-, 2- or 3-param handler is dispatched by Express identically to before.

The global handler in `server/index.ts:305` is an arrow with 4 params registered through the patched `app.use` (registerRoutes runs at line 199, so the patch is live by then) — it is passed through unwrapped. Verified end-to-end over HTTP, not just by inspection.

## The already-responded case

The guard **never writes a response** — it only calls `next(err)`. The global handler is the single decision point, and I verified its `!res.headersSent` check actually covers both patterns rather than assuming:

- **Fast-ack webhooks** (`res.status(200).send("OK")` before the `try`): I asserted on **raw socket bytes**, not through an HTTP client that would hide a second response. Exactly one `HTTP/1.1` status line, body ends at `OK`, no error text, and the error handler confirms it ran with `headersSent === true`.
- **SSE**: I added a direct test that `res.headersSent` flips to `true` *immediately* on `writeHead` (`[false, true]`) — that's the load-bearing assumption, so it's asserted rather than trusted. The stream test then confirms the raw bytes end at the last chunk frame, contain no `{"message"` body, no second status line, and **no terminating chunk** — i.e. the stream is still open and uncorrupted.

Two related subtleties I handled: a rejection with a falsy reason would make Express read `next(undefined)` as "no error, keep routing" and the request would still hang; and the strings `"route"`/`"router"` are Express flow-control signals. Those four cases are boxed into a real `Error` (original kept on `.cause`). Everything else forwards untouched, so custom errors carrying `status`/`statusCode` still reach the handler with their status intact (tested: a 402 stays a 402).

## Two judgement calls worth flagging

1. **`isPromise` is narrow on purpose.** A duck-typed `typeof value.then === "function"` would be wrong here: Drizzle query builders are thenable *and lazy* — calling `.then` executes the query. A handler that returned one without awaiting would have had its query fired a second time by the guard. I confirmed Drizzle sets `[Symbol.toStringTag] = "QueryPromise"` (`node_modules/drizzle-orm/query-promise.js:4`) and match only `instanceof Promise` or `[object Promise]`. Every handler in the risk class is an `async function`, which always returns a native promise, so nothing in scope is lost. There's a test asserting a Drizzle-shaped lazy thenable is never subscribed to.
2. **Sub-apps and routers are passed through unwrapped.** Express detects them by `fn.handle && fn.set` (sub-app) / `.stack` (router); wrapping would hide those and demote them to plain middleware, losing `mountpath`, the `mount` event and `req.app` restoration. They never return a promise. This also means `vite.middlewares` (a connect app) is untouched.

Idempotency is enforced at both levels via `Symbol.for` flags — realm-global, so it holds even if the module is loaded twice under tsx vs ts-jest.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — **clean, exit 0**. (An earlier run showed syntax errors in `server/migrate.ts`; that's another agent's untracked file caught mid-write, and it cleared on its own.)
- `npx jest --selectProjects server --runInBand` — **19 suites, 303 tests, all passing.**

**`/home/runner/workspace/server/__tests__/async-route-guard.test.ts`** (new, 31 tests). No supertest in `package.json` and I didn't add it — the tests drive a real `node:http` server on an ephemeral port, with `node:net` for the raw-byte assertions. Coverage: an A/B pair proving the *same* handler hangs without the guard (400ms timeout) and returns 500 with it; throw-after-await; status preservation; the four odd rejection reasons; all seven patched methods; 4-arity error middleware working end-to-end; arity preserved for 0–3 and identity for ≥4; sync handlers untouched (including that a sync throw still propagates and is *not* swallowed); multiple/nested/array handlers in order; `app.get(setting)`; chaining returns `app`; sub-app + router mounting; `this`/args forwarding; lazy thenables; double-install; and a static check that the install call precedes the first route in `routes.ts` (matching the house pattern of `subscription-route-security.test.ts`, which reads routes.ts as text rather than importing it).

## What I could not verify

- **The running app.** The dev server is a supervised `tsx server/index.ts` with no watch, so it's still executing pre-change code, and I was told not to restart it. My verification is against a real Express 4.21.2 server with a byte-for-byte copy of the index.ts:305 handler — not the actual app boot. Worth one manual reload before you trust it in anger.
- **Coverage boundary:** middleware registered in `server/index.ts` *before* `registerRoutes` (helmet, compression, urlencoded, the request logger — lines 27–91) is not covered. Extending it there would mean editing a file another agent owns.
- **Pre-existing ordering nuance, unchanged by me:** the global error handler is registered at index.ts:305, but `setupVite`/`serveStatic` and the crawler middleware register *after* it, so errors originating in those layers still bypass it and reach `finalhandler`. Vite's catch-all already try/catches and calls `next(e)` itself, so nothing regresses — just noting it isn't fixed either.
- **Double-`next` interleaving:** a handler that calls `next()` and *then* rejects will also get `next(err)`. It cannot double-send (the `headersSent` check), but I did not exhaustively reason through every routing interleaving. No handler in the codebase does this today; it would already be a bug.
- Baseline test count was 199 in this working tree, not the 188 you quoted — other agents added `server/__tests__/migrate.test.ts` and touched `auth-core-regressions.test.ts` while I worked. All of it is green.

I did not stage, commit, or touch anything outside those three files.</result>

1. **Per-attempt `AbortController` + timer** (4s) — covers the response body too, not just headers.
2. **Bounded attempt count** — 3 attempts max, fixed delays `[300, 900]`. Retries only for retryable outcomes; a 404 doesn't retry at all.

- **Never truncate or seed over live data.** The `seedDatabase()` function in `server/seed.ts` has a guard that exits immediately if any merchants exist. This guard must never be removed. Stock items, transactions, and merchant records must never be deleted or replaced by any startup routine.

input.new_string:
- **Nothing syncs the schema on startup.** Starting the server does **not** apply schema changes. The `drizzle-kit push` block in `server/index.ts` only runs when `RUN_SCHEMA_PUSH=true` or `RUN_MIGRATIONS=true` is set, which is normally off. Adding a column to `shared/schema.ts` and restarting therefore changes nothing in the database — and because Drizzle's `select()` lists every declared column, the *code* will then query a column the database does not have and every read of that table fails. On 2026-08-09 this took the whole app down: `/api/auth/me` threw, and since first paint is gated on it, every device sat on a loading spinner.
- **Apply schema changes as numbered SQL migrations.** Write additive SQL in `migrations/`, then run `npm run db:migrate`. `npm run db:migrate:status` reports applied/pending/drifted; the server logs a loud warning at startup if anything is pending but never applies it by itself. Adopting the runner on a database that already has the effects is `npm run db:migrate:baseline -- --confirm`. Both dev and production were baselined at 15 migrations on 2026-08-09.
- **Never use `--force` with `drizzle-kit push`, and prefer not to use push at all.** It reports the FK columns that were created as `serial` (`transactions.merchant_id`, `platform_fees.transaction_id`, `refunds.transaction_id`) as destructive changes and offers to truncate those tables. Without `--force` it refuses and exits non-zero rather than destroying data. Use a migration instead.
- **Never truncate or seed over live data.** The `seedDatabase()` function in `server/seed.ts` has a guard that exits immediately if any merchants exist. This guard must never be removed. Stock items, transactions, and merchant records must never be deleted or replaced by any startup routine.
- **`migrations/` is not yet a complete schema history.** Nine tables and a number of `merchants`/`invoices_rent_requests` columns exist in the databases but are created by no migration — they arrived via `drizzle-kit push` and the ad-hoc `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` blocks in `server/index.ts`. The runner guarantees nothing is missed going forward, but the database cannot yet be rebuilt from `migrations/` alone.
